text:
Enoshima has a paid escalator to the top of the island: ¥500 for three sections that replace about 20 minutes of stone steps. What nobody tells you is that it only goes up 👇

🎯 Guess how we'd get back down without the stairs, then check our answer 👉 https://japanbystation.com/enoshima-without-the-stairs

We put this together for anyone travelling with a parent or partner who walks happily on the flat but tires on long stairways. We checked every price and time against the operators' own pages before writing a word.

🏝️ THREE WAYS TO DO IT

1️⃣ Lower island only. Walk the flat 389 m Benten Bridge, stroll the shop street, and make a long shirasu lunch the goal. No climbing at all, and Fuji can show up over the water from the bridge on clear days.

2️⃣ Escalator up, boat back. Ride the Escar to the Samuel Cocking Garden and the Sea Candle, walk on to the rocks at Chigogafuchi, then take the little Benten-maru boat back to the bridge in about 10 minutes. Kanagawa's own tourism page suggests the boat for the way back to save energy.

3️⃣ Stay on the shore. The walk from Katase-Enoshima Station to the aquarium was checked by Kanagawa's tourism board and is usable even by powered wheelchair. Add Katase West Beach, one of the official Fuji viewpoints.

🌊 OUR TAKE

Plan 2 on a calm day. The boat has no timetable and stops in rough seas, so phone before 10:00 on the morning you go. If it's not running, plan 1 or 3 still makes a lovely half day from Tokyo.

👉 The flat Fuji viewpoint most people walk straight past, plus the full stair-light route:
https://japanbystation.com/enoshima-without-the-stairs

Which would your travel partner choose: escalator and boat, or a long lunch by the bridge? 🍚
